fact_statement: Joseph Lister applied carbolic acid dressings to open compound fractures in Glasgow to eliminate post-surgical bacterial infection.
ground_truth: Joseph Lister introduced carbolic acid antiseptic treatment for surgical instruments and compound fractures in Glasgow hospital wards.

fact_statement: Louis Pasteur developed the process of pasteurization in France to kill pathogenic microbes in wine and milk through controlled heat.
ground_truth: Louis Pasteur invented pasteurization by applying controlled thermal processing to eliminate harmful bacteria in liquids.

fact_statement: Robert Koch formulated his four scientific postulates in Germany to establish causal relationships between specific microorganisms and clinical diseases.
ground_truth: Robert Koch established four specific experimental criteria designed to prove that a particular microorganism causes a given disease.

fact_statement: Alexander Fleming noted that Penicillium notatum mould dissolved staphylococci bacteria colonies in a laboratory culture dish in 1928.
ground_truth: Alexander Fleming observed that colonies of staphylococci bacteria were destroyed by contaminating Penicillium mould in his laboratory.

fact_statement: Edward Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with cowpox fluid in 1796 to provide immunity against smallpox.
ground_truth: Edward Jenner successfully protected young James Phipps from smallpox by inoculating him with material from cowpox lesions.

fact_statement: William Harvey studied animal heart contractions to prove that blood flows in a continuous circuit through arteries and veins.
ground_truth: William Harvey conducted anatomical dissections on animals to prove that the heart pumps blood through a closed circulatory system.

fact_statement: Florence Nightingale gathered statistical data on soldier deaths in Scutari to demonstrate that sanitary improvements reduced military hospital mortality.
ground_truth: Florence Nightingale used statistical diagrams in Scutari to show that infectious diseases caused more deaths than battlefield wounds.

fact_statement: Jonas Salk evaluated his inactivated polio vaccine in a 1954 nationwide trial involving over 1.8 million American schoolchildren.
ground_truth: Jonas Salk conducted massive clinical field trials in 1954 involving 1.8 million children to test the inactivated polio vaccine.

fact_statement: Albert Sabin tested his live attenuated oral polio vaccine internationally in the Soviet Union during the late 1950s.
ground_truth: Albert Sabin conducted large-scale clinical trials of his oral polio vaccine in the Soviet Union during the late 1950s.

fact_statement: Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine using material from cowpox lesions. His work built upon earlier practices of variolation and established the field of vaccinology.
ground_truth: Edward Jenner created the first smallpox vaccine using cowpox virus material. His breakthrough in 1796 laid the foundation for modern preventive immunology and widespread immunization programs.

fact_statement: Louis Pasteur refuted the theory of spontaneous generation through swan-neck flask experiments. He subsequently formulated the germ theory of disease alongside Robert Koch.
ground_truth: Louis Pasteur disproved spontaneous generation using specially designed swan-neck flasks. He later established the germ theory of disease, demonstrating that specific microbes cause infectious illnesses.

fact_statement: Joseph Lister observed high post-operative mortality from surgical ward gangrene. He introduced carbolic acid spray and sterilized instruments to eliminate bacterial infection during operations.
ground_truth: Joseph Lister identified microbial contamination as the root cause of wound sepsis after surgery. He pioneered antiseptic surgery by applying carbolic acid solutions to wounds, instruments, and dressings.

fact_statement: Alexander Fleming noticed a halo of inhibited bacteria around Penicillium mould in 1928. Ernst Chain and Howard Florey later isolated the antibiotic compound for clinical use during World War II.
ground_truth: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 after observing mould kill bacteria on a culture plate. Howard Florey and Ernst Chain subsequently mass-produced the drug for therapeutic medical use.

fact_statement: In 1854, John Snow tracked cholera deaths in London's Soho district. His mapping identified over 500 fatal cases clustered within 250 yards of the Broad Street pump within ten days.
ground_truth: John Snow investigated the 1854 London cholera outbreak by mapping mortality patterns across Soho streets. He documented over 500 fatal infections located within a short distance of the Broad Street water pump over a ten-day period.

fact_statement: In 1948, the World Health Assembly established its first budget at $5 million. By the 2025–2026 biennium, the World Health Organization's approved budget grew to $6.83 billion.
ground_truth: The inaugural World Health Assembly approved an initial budget of $5 million for 1949. Decades later, the World Health Organization's biennial budget reached $6.83 billion for 2025–2026.

fact_statement: Robert Koch isolated Bacillus anthracis in 1876 and later identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis in 1882. These discoveries earned him the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1905.
ground_truth: Robert Koch demonstrated the bacterial cause of anthrax in 1876 and identified the tuberculosis bacillus in 1882. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his tuberculosis research in 1905.

fact_statement: Jonas Salk developed the inactivated polio vaccine in 1952. Following extensive field trials, the vaccine was officially licensed for widespread public administration in 1955.
ground_truth: Jonas Salk created the first inactivated poliovirus vaccine in 1952. After nationwide testing involving 1.8 million children, the vaccine was declared safe and licensed in 1955.

fact_statement: The 1978 International Conference on Primary Health Care was hosted in Alma-Ata, Kazakh SSR. The resulting declaration asserted that health is a fundamental human right.
ground_truth: Delegates gathered in Alma-Ata, Kazakh SSR, for a landmark international conference in 1978. The resulting Alma-Ata Declaration declared health to be a core human right and prioritized primary healthcare.

fact_statement: Ignaz Semmelweis worked at the Vienna General Hospital in the 1840s. He observed that doctors transferring from autopsy rooms carried cadaverous particles that caused puerperal fever in maternity wards.
ground_truth: While serving at the Vienna General Hospital in the 1840s, Ignaz Semmelweis linked fatal puerperal fever to unwashed hands. He discovered that medical personnel carried cadaverous material directly from autopsy tables to women in labor.

fact_statement: William Harvey published De Motu Cordis in Frankfurt in 1628. He proved through dissection that cardiac valves ensure unidirectional blood flow through a continuous vascular system.
ground_truth: William Harvey published his landmark circulatory treatise De Motu Cordis in 1628. Through experimental dissections, he proved that the heart functions as a muscular pump driving blood in a single direction through closed vessels.

fact_statement: Florence Nightingale instituted clean laundry, proper ventilation, and improved drainage at Scutari hospital during the Crimean War. Her reforms reduced the hospital mortality rate from 42% to 2%.
ground_truth: Florence Nightingale introduced strict sanitation, ventilation, and hygienic standards at the Scutari military hospital during the Crimean War. Her interventions dramatically reduced patient death rates from over 40% down to approximately 2%.

fact_statement: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays at the University of Würzburg in November 1895. He produced the first medical radiographic image showing the bones of his wife's hand.
ground_truth: Wilhelm Röntgen identified X-radiation while experimenting with vacuum tubes at the University of Würzburg in 1895. He created the world's first medical radiograph by capturing an image of his wife's hand on a photographic plate.

fact_statement: Karl Landsteiner discovered the A, B, and O human blood groups in Vienna in 1901. His discovery enabled safe blood transfusions and earned him the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
ground_truth: Karl Landsteiner identified the main ABO blood group systems in 1901 while working in Vienna. His classification system made blood transfusions safe for patients and won him the Nobel Prize in 1930.

fact_statement: The Swiss physician who pioneered modern surgical antisepsis through rigorous thyroid pathology studies was Theodor Kocher.
ground_truth: Theodor Kocher received the Nobel Prize for his groundbreaking surgical and pathological work on the thyroid gland.

fact_statement: The French scientist who established anaerobic bacteriology and discovered Clostridium butyricum was Louis Pasteur.
ground_truth: Louis Pasteur discovered anaerobic microorganisms capable of living without free atmospheric oxygen.

fact_statement: The German physician who discovered the diphtheria antitoxin alongside Kitasato Shibasaburo was Emil von Behring.
ground_truth: Emil von Behring developed blood serum therapy against diphtheria, earning the first Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

fact_statement: The British physician who proved that cholera was transmitted through contaminated water supplies rather than miasma was John Snow.
ground_truth: John Snow demonstrated waterborne transmission of cholera, refuting the dominant miasma theory of disease spread.

fact_statement: The Roman encyclopedist who compiled De Medicina, detailing ancient surgical techniques and medical knowledge, was Aulus Cornelius Celsus.
ground_truth: Aulus Cornelius Celsus authored De Medicina, providing a major comprehensive source of Roman medical knowledge.

fact_statement: The World Health Organization recognizes 6 official regional offices operating across different geopolitical zones worldwide.
ground_truth: The World Health Organization manages global operations through six decentralized regional offices.

fact_statement: The total number of essential amino acids required by the human body through diet is 9.
ground_truth: The human body requires nine essential amino acids that cannot be synthesized internally and must come from food.

fact_statement: The inaugural World Health Assembly convened in Geneva in 1948 with delegates representing 53 member states.
ground_truth: Delegates from 53 member nations gathered at the first World Health Assembly held in 1948.

fact_statement: According to global public health targets, Sustainable Development Goal 3 includes 13 specific health targets.
ground_truth: Sustainable Development Goal 3 comprises 13 distinct targets designed to ensure healthy lives worldwide.

fact_statement: The Pan American Health Organization was established under its original name, the International Sanitary Bureau, in 1902.
ground_truth: The International Sanitary Bureau was formally established in 1902, later evolving into the Pan American Health Organization.

fact_statement: The World Health Organization launched its global Expanded Programme on Immunization in 1974.
ground_truth: The Expanded Programme on Immunization was initiated by the World Health Organization in 1974 to protect children against vaccine-preventable diseases.

fact_statement: The headquarters of the World Health Organization Regional Office for South-East Asia is located in New Delhi.
ground_truth: New Delhi hosts the regional headquarters for the World Health Organization South-East Asia Region.

fact_statement: The headquarters of the World Health Organization Regional Office for Africa is established in Brazzaville.
ground_truth: The World Health Organization Regional Office for Africa maintains its primary headquarters in Brazzaville.

fact_statement: Paul Ehrlich developed Arsphenamine in Germany to treat syphilis through targeted chemical chemotherapy.
ground_truth: Paul Ehrlich synthesized Arsphenamine to target Treponema pallidum infections selectively without killing patient host cells.

fact_statement: Gerhard Domagk discovered Prontosil in Germany as the first commercially available synthetic antibacterial sulfonamide.
ground_truth: Gerhard Domagk identified the antimicrobial efficacy of Prontosil, initiating the era of synthetic sulfonamide antibiotics.

fact_statement: The Global Polio Eradication Initiative was formed in 1988 by international health bodies to eradicate wild poliovirus transmission.
ground_truth: In 1988, international health leadership formed the Global Polio Eradication Initiative to achieve complete wild poliovirus eradication.

fact_statement: The Framework Convention on Tobacco Control was adopted in Geneva in 2003 under World Health Organization governance.
ground_truth: The World Health Organization adopted the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control in 2003 to combat global tobacco-related illness.

fact_statement: The International Sanitary Conferences began meeting in Paris in 1851 to standardize international quarantine standards against cholera epidemics.
ground_truth: The inaugural International Sanitary Conference convened in Paris in 1851 to negotiate international maritime quarantine protocols against cholera.

fact_statement: Emil von Behring discovered blood serum diphtheria antitoxins while working in Germany. His immunologic research earned him the first Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1901.
ground_truth: Emil von Behring demonstrated serum therapy for treating diphtheria in Germany. His breakthrough in diphtheria antitoxin research led to his selection as the inaugural Nobel laureate in Physiology or Medicine in 1901.

fact_statement: Paul Ehrlich formulated the receptor theory of immunity in Germany. He went on to synthesize Salvarsan, founding selective chemical chemotherapy.
ground_truth: Paul Ehrlich advanced the side-chain theory of cellular immunity while researching in Germany. He later developed Salvarsan as a targeted antimicrobial agent, establishing modern chemical therapeutics.

fact_statement: In 1988, the World Health Assembly resolved to eradicate poliomyelitis when wild poliovirus infected over 350,000 children annually. By 2001, global annual reported cases fell below 1,000.
ground_truth: The World Health Assembly targeted global polio eradication in 1988 when endemic poliovirus paralyzed an estimated 350,000 children per year. Extensive vaccination reduced annual global incidence under 1,000 cases by 2001.

fact_statement: The World Health Organization adopted its first global public health treaty in 2003. This treaty, the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, officially entered into force in 2005.
ground_truth: The World Health Assembly adopted the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control in 2003. Following international ratification, the binding public health treaty came into force legally in 2005.

fact_statement: The Pan American Health Organization maintains its headquarters in Washington, D.C. It functions as the specialized health agency for the Inter-American System and serves as the WHO Regional Office for the Americas.
ground_truth: The Pan American Health Organization operates its central office out of Washington, D.C. It serves as the dedicated regional health arm for the Americas under the World Health Organization framework.

fact_statement: Gerhard Domagk tested Prontosil on bacterial infections in Germany during 1932. His discovery demonstrated that azo dyes could act as systemic antibacterial agents in living organisms.
ground_truth: Gerhard Domagk discovered the antibacterial activity of the synthetic dye Prontosil in Germany in 1932. His laboratory tests proved that sulfonamides could selectively kill bacteria inside living animal hosts.

fact_statement: The Office International d'Hygiène Publique was founded in Paris in 1907. It established early international epidemiological surveillance for cholera, plague, and yellow fever before being absorbed by the World Health Organization.
ground_truth: Established in Paris in 1907, the Office International d'Hygiène Publique monitored global pestilential disease outbreaks. Its health surveillance mechanisms were later incorporated into the World Health Organization upon its creation.
